# sRtr

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/sRtr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/sRtr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)
![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)
<!-- badges: end -->

The **sRtr** package provides tools to load, label, and work with the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) Standard Analysis Files (SAFs) in R. It supports automatic variable labeling and factor conversion using the official SRTR data dictionary.

## What do you want to do?

- [Load my first SRTR file](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/sRtr/articles/getting-started.html#install-and-load)
- [Link candidate, transplant, and follow-up files](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/sRtr/articles/files-and-keys.html)
- [Build a cohort and track exclusions](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/sRtr/articles/building-cohort-with-flowchart.html)
- [Define rejection, malignancy, graft failure, or death](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/sRtr/articles/follow-up-forms.html#which-section-answers-your-question)
- [Map transplant centers and service areas](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/sRtr/articles/mapping.html)

Every guide is listed in the [article index](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/sRtr/articles/index.html), and every function in the [function reference](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/sRtr/reference/index.html). To help develop sRtr, see [Development and how to contribute](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/sRtr/articles/development.html).

## Installation

You can install the development version of **sRtr** from [GitHub](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/sRtr) with:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("VagishHemmige/sRtr")
```

## A first load

Point sRtr at the folder that holds your SAFs, then load a file with its factor and variable labels:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(sRtr)

set_srtr_wd("path/to/srtr/files")
# or remember the folder for later sessions:
# set_srtr_wd("path/to/srtr/files", permanent = TRUE)

tx_li <- load_srtr_file("TX_LI")
```

[Getting started](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/sRtr/articles/getting-started.html) goes on from here: how sRtr finds your release, what the labels and codes mean, how to join files, and how to share results safely.
